title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
summary: Multi-author report deriving computational 'indicator properties' of consciousness from RPT, GWT, higher-order, predictive-processing and attention-schema theories, then assessing existing AI systems against them. Reports that no current AI system is a strong candidate for consciousness, while finding no obvious technical barrier to implementing the indicators. Explicitly adopts computational functionalism as a working hypothesis.
limitations: Preprint, not peer-reviewed at time of access.
The rubric is explicitly described by its authors as provisional.
Assesses only a small number of existing systems (LLMs, Perceiver, DeepMind Adaptive Agent, PaLM-E).
Deliberately excludes IIT because IIT is not compatible with computational functionalism -- so this source is NOT a neutral survey of all major theories.
bears_on: Primary source for CE-1's indicator-property rubric. Also the source of a factual error in research/RESEARCH_MAP.md: that file lists IIT alongside GWT/RPT/HOT/PP as a parallel candidate without noting that the principal AI-consciousness indicator framework deliberately excludes IIT.

title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
summary: Preregistered open-science adversarial collaboration directly juxtaposing IIT and GNWT, with theory proponents separated from data acquisition and analysis. n=256 participants; fMRI (n=120), MEG (n=102), iEEG (n=34); three preregistered predictions with pass/fail criteria agreed ex ante. Found conscious-content information in visual, ventrotemporal and inferior frontal cortex. Challenged IIT: absence of sustained content-specific posterior-cortex synchronisation predicted by IIT (Bayes factor 1.15-4.9 for the null). Challenged GNWT: general lack of ignition at stimulus offset, and limited representation of identity/orientation in prefrontal cortex. Authors explicitly decline to render a single verdict and invite readers to weigh the evidence.
limitations: Human subjects only -- results do not transfer directly to artificial architectures.
iEEG sampled 12 V1/V2 electrodes versus 472 PFC electrodes, an acknowledged sampling asymmetry.
Three stimuli and a restricted phenomenal space; the authors note the design 'falls short of encompassing its full phenomenal richness'.
The authors note that residual task engagement cannot be entirely ruled out for category.
bears_on: The strongest single empirical datum for CE-1's Stage 4 (theory-specific predictions): a preregistered head-to-head that CHALLENGED BOTH leading theories rather than confirming one. Directly relevant to research/THEORY_COMPARISON.md. Note it invalidates any assumption that one theory is the settled winner.

title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: Formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
summary: Formal statement of IIT 4.0: identifies axioms of experience, infers the necessary-and-sufficient postulates any substrate must satisfy, and expresses them mathematically. The authors claim testable predictions about both presence and quality of experience, and propose that the postulates be applied to any system of units in a state in order to determine whether and to what degree that system is conscious. That last proposition is IIT's own claim, recorded here as an attributed source claim; CE-1 does not adopt it.
limitations: Read at abstract and citation level plus the published summary; the 45-page formal derivation was not worked through line by line.
The central quantity (phi) is computationally intractable for systems of realistic size, which is the main practical obstacle to applying it to large artificial networks.

Notably, the Cogitate consortium (cogitate2025) found IIT's preregistered posterior-cortex connectivity prediction was not met -- so this theory's central empirical claim is currently contested, not settled.
Proponent-authored: Tononi and Boly are IIT architects and were also adversaries in cogitate2025, so they are not disinterested parties to that test.
bears_on: Reference statement of the theory that research/RESEARCH_MAP.md describes only as 'mathematically rigorous but computationally intractable' without noting it was also empirically challenged in 2025.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
summary: Introduces virtual context management: an OS-inspired memory hierarchy in which the LLM manages a main context window and pages information in and out of external storage via function calls, providing an illusion of extended memory on a fixed-context model. Evaluated on document analysis and multi-session chat, reporting that MemGPT outperforms prior LLM-based approaches in both.
limitations: Explicitly frames memory as paging between tiers -- architecturally this is retrieval and eviction, which is the mechanism CE-1's own audit shows is confounded with prompt-length effects when used as an H1 test.
The paper's own framing ('illusion of an extended context') is a caution against reading persistence into what is fundamentally a context-management scheme.
Evaluation is on document analysis and chat, not on any measure bearing on subjective experience.
bears_on: Canonical citation for the Letta/MemGPT system listed in research/RESEARCH_MAP.md section 2, which currently has no citation at all. Establishes that agent-managed tiered memory exists and is well documented -- while remaining squarely in the 'retrieval' category that Section 4C of the master directive asks CE-1 to distinguish from genuinely integrated cognitive architecture.
